examples.en: He is just an observer watching the incident.

examples.ko: 관찰자의 눈으로 보면 문제가 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you look through an observer's eyes, the problem is easier to see.
In the study an observer records the children's behavior.
I attended this meeting as an observer.

examples.ko: 좋은 관찰자는 작은 변화도 놓치지 않아요.
examples.en: A good observer doesn't miss even small changes.
I sat quietly like an observer and watched the people.

explain: 관찰자는 직접 하지 않고 곁에서 보며 살피는 사람이에요. '구경꾼'은 재미로 보는 사람이고, '목격자'는 사건을 직접 본 사람이에요. 관찰자는 연구나 회의처럼 일부러 살펴보는 자리에서 주로 써요.

phrases.en: I watched the meeting from an observer's position.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 하지 않고 곁에서 보는 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the position of watching from the side rather than taking part.

phrases.en: Today I became an observer and watched the class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 살펴보는 역할을 맡을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking on a role of watching on purpose.

phrases.en: An outside observer attended the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직 밖에서 온 사람이 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone from outside the group comes to observe.

explain_en: A 관찰자 watches closely from the side without taking part. A '구경꾼' watches for fun, and a '목격자' is someone who saw an incident firsthand. 관찰자 is mostly used where watching is deliberate, like research or meetings.

examples.en: The event winners will be announced next week.
Winners will be contacted by text message.
I became a winner of that event!
I checked the list of winners on the website.
There are only ten winners, so the competition is fierce.
The winners drawn by lottery came up on stage.

explain: 추첨이나 응모에서 뽑힌 사람이에요. '당첨되다'(뽑히다)와 같이 알아 두면 좋아요. '당첨자'는 이벤트·청약·복권에 두루 쓰이고, 실력으로 이긴 사람은 '우승자'나 '수상자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The winners are announced on Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이벤트 결과를 알릴 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for announcing event results.

phrases.en: I checked the winner list on the website.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽑힌 사람의 이름을 모은 목록을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the list of selected names.

phrases.en: I won the event drawing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '당첨자'가 되는 동작을 동사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for becoming a 당첨자.
phrases.en_equiv: to be selected as a winner

explain_en: The person drawn in a lottery or sweepstakes. Learn it with '당첨되다' (be picked). It covers events, housing lotteries and lotto; someone who wins by skill is '우승자' or '수상자'.

examples.en: My grandfather passed away yesterday.
They say that writer passed away last month.
I heard the news that our teacher passed away.
The house has been quiet since grandmother passed away.

examples.ko: 신문에 어느 유명 배우가 별세했다는 기사가 났어요.
examples.en: A newspaper article said a famous actor had passed away.
Everyone observed a moment of silence for the person who passed away.

explain: '별세하다'는 윗사람이나 존경하는 분이 돌아가셨을 때 쓰는 높임말이에요. 보통 '별세하셨어요'처럼 '-시-'를 넣어요. 가족에게도 쓰지만 일상 대화에서는 '돌아가셨어요'가 더 자연스럽고, 친구나 동물에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: My grandfather passed away last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별세하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in everyday conversation than '별세하다'.

phrases.en: I heard the news of my teacher's passing today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 공식 인사에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news and in formal condolences.

phrases.en: I prayed for the person who passed away last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-시-'를 넣어 존경하는 마음을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-시-' shows respect for the person.

explain_en: 별세하다 is an honorific for when an elder or respected person has died, usually with -시- as in 별세하셨어요. It can be used for family too, but in daily conversation 돌아가셨어요 is more natural. It is not used for friends or animals.

p.n: 돌아가시다 is softer and more conversational.

examples.ko: 저는 이 라디오 프로그램의 오랜 애청자예요.
examples.en: I'm a longtime regular listener of this radio show.
A listener's story was featured on today's broadcast.

examples.ko: 이 팟캐스트는 애청자가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: This podcast is gaining more and more regular listeners.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 그 드라마의 열혈 애청자라서 한 회도 안 놓쳐요.
examples.en: My friend is such a devoted viewer of that drama that she never misses an episode.

examples.ko: 애청자 여러분, 오늘도 방송을 들어 주셔서 감사해요.
examples.en: Dear listeners, thank you for tuning in again today.

examples.ko: 라디오 애청자라면 이 목소리를 바로 알 거예요.
examples.en: If you're a regular radio listener, you'll recognize this voice right away.

explain: '시청자'는 TV를 보는 사람, '청취자'는 라디오를 듣는 사람이고, '애청자'는 거기에 '즐겨 듣고 본다'는 마음이 더해진 말이에요. 라디오, 팟캐스트, 드라마처럼 방송에 주로 쓰고, 책이나 신문을 즐겨 읽는 사람은 '애독자'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 애청자 여러분, 오늘도 들어 주셔서 감사해요.
phrases.en: Dear listeners, thank you for tuning in today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송에서 청취자에게 인사할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A greeting to listeners used on broadcasts.

phrases.en: I am a regular viewer of that drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 즐겨 보는 방송 프로그램 이름과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the name of a show you regularly watch.

phrases.en: I heard that show and became a regular listener.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아서 계속 듣게 된 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes becoming a loyal listener after liking a show.

explain_en: '시청자' is someone who watches TV and '청취자' is someone who listens to the radio; '애청자' adds the feeling of watching or listening because you enjoy it. It is mostly used for broadcasts such as radio, podcasts and dramas. For someone who loves reading books or newspapers, people say '애독자'.

examples.en: The bereaved family quietly received guests at the funeral hall.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 사고 유족을 위한 모금이 시작됐다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says a fundraiser for the families of the accident victims has started.
I offered words of comfort to the bereaved family.
A representative of the bereaved families held a press conference.

examples.ko: 정부가 유족을 돕는 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is looking for ways to help the bereaved families.

examples.ko: 유족은 그날의 일을 지금도 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: The bereaved family still cannot forget what happened that day.

explain: 유족은 돌아가신 분의 가족을 말해요. 그냥 '가족'이라고 하면 평소의 가족이고, 유족은 누군가가 세상을 떠난 뒤에만 써요. 장례식장·뉴스·사고 기사에서 자주 나오고, 보통 '유족 여러분', '유족에게'처럼 정중하게 말해요.

phrases.en: The bereaved family members gave an interview on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유족'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 뉴스에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 유족, and more common in news reports.

phrases.en: The friends offered words of comfort to the bereaved family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위로나 도움을 전할 때 쓰는 정중한 조사 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to say who comfort or help is given to.

phrases.en: A group to help the families of accident victims was formed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일로 가족을 잃었는지 '사고'를 붙여 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 사고 says what kind of loss the family had.

explain_en: 유족 is the family left behind by someone who has died. '가족' is family in general, while 유족 is used only after a death. It appears at funerals and in accident news, usually in polite phrasing such as '유족에게'.

examples.ko: 통계청 조사원이 집을 방문해서 가구 구성과 소득을 물어봤어요.
examples.en: A Statistics Office surveyor visited my home and asked about household members and income.
The surveyor showed his ID first.

examples.ko: 저는 인구 조사원으로 일한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once worked as a census surveyor.
Please answer the surveyor's questions honestly.
I saw a notice recruiting surveyors on the internet.
Surveyors go around the village asking for people's opinions.

explain: 설문이나 통계를 위해 사람들을 만나 물어보고 기록하는 사람이에요. '조사관'은 사건이나 위반을 조사하는 공무원에게 써서 느낌이 달라요. 보통 '인구 조사원', '여론 조사원'처럼 앞에 조사 종류를 붙여요.

phrases.en: A census taker came to our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인구를 조사하는 사람이고, 앞에 조사 종류를 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is someone who surveys the population, with the survey type placed first.

phrases.en: A pollster asked questions by phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 생각을 묻는 일을 하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a person whose job is to ask people their opinions.

phrases.en: I answered the surveyor's questions one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사를 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is said from the point of view of the person being surveyed.

explain_en: It is a person who meets people to ask questions and record answers for surveys or statistics. '조사관' is used for officials who investigate cases or violations, so it feels different. People usually put the kind of survey in front, like '인구 조사원' or '여론 조사원'.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 오래된 종족이 살고 있어요.
examples.en: An ancient tribe lives on this island.
That tribe uses its own language.
I watched a documentary about a tribe's way of life.
Each tribe has different traditional clothing.
The song of the forest tribe was beautiful.

examples.ko: 종족을 지키려고 마을 사람들이 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: The villagers joined forces to protect their people.

explain: 종족은 같은 조상, 말, 풍습을 가진 사람들의 무리예요. 게임이나 판타지에서는 사람, 엘프처럼 나뉜 무리를 종족이라고 불러요. 비슷한 말로 '부족'이 있는데, 부족은 한 지역에서 함께 사는 작은 공동체를 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 섬에는 여러 종족이 함께 살아요.
phrases.en: Several ethnic groups live together on that island.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여러'를 붙여 서로 다른 종족이 여럿 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 여러 says that there are several different groups.

phrases.en: Each tribe has a different culture.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마다'를 붙여 종족 하나하나가 다르다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 마다 means each and every group.

phrases.example: 이 게임에서는 어떤 종족을 고를 거예요?
phrases.en: Which race will you choose in this game?
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임이나 판타지에서 사람, 엘프 같은 종류를 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in games and fantasy for choosing a race such as human or elf.

explain_en: 종족 is a group of people sharing ancestors, language, and customs. In games and fantasy, groups like humans or elves are also called 종족. A similar word is '부족', which means a small community living together in one area.

en: adviser; staff member who advises a leader

examples.en: The president's advisers held an emergency meeting.

examples.ko: 좋은 참모가 있으면 리더가 더 잘 결정해요.
examples.en: With good advisers, a leader decides better.
He is an adviser who is like the boss's right hand.

examples.ko: 선거 캠프의 참모로 일한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once worked as an adviser on an election campaign.
I changed the plan after hearing my adviser.
The advisory staff held a meeting all night.

explain: '비서'는 일정과 문서를 챙기는 사람이고, '참모'는 방향과 전략에 대해 조언하는 사람이에요. 정치·군대·회사 뉴스에서 주로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 비유로만 써요. 여러 명이면 '참모진'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The president's team of advisers announced a new plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참모 여러 명을 한 팀으로 묶어 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a group of advisers as one team.

phrases.en: He is the boss's key adviser.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 가까이서 중요한 조언을 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the adviser who gives the most important counsel.

phrases.en: He works as the mayor's adviser.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조언하는 역할로 일한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means working in an advisory role.

explain_en: A '비서' manages schedules and documents; a '참모' advises on direction and strategy. It mainly appears in political, military, and corporate news, and in daily talk only figuratively. A group of them is '참모진'.

examples.en: That poet was born in Busan in 1920.
When a baby is born, you have to report it to the district office.

examples.ko: 출생한 지 일주일 된 아기를 안아 봤어요.
examples.en: I held a baby who was one week old.
I was born in Seoul and have lived here ever since.
I heard the twins were born an hour apart.

examples.ko: 이 서류에는 출생할 때 몸무게를 적어요.
examples.en: On this form you write the weight at birth.

explain: 일상에서는 '태어나다'를 쓰고, 출생하다는 서류, 뉴스, 인물 소개에서 써요. 친구에게 '저는 부산에서 출생했어요'라고 하면 딱딱하게 들려요. '부산에서 태어났어요'가 자연스러워요. '출생지', '출생 신고'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 아기가 태어나면 출생 신고를 해야 해요.
phrases.en: When a baby is born, you have to register the birth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류와 관련된 일에서 자주 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun pairing often used in paperwork contexts.

phrases.en: Please write your birthplace on the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태어난 곳을 서류나 소개에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the place of birth in forms or introductions.

phrases.en: I was born in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 출생하다 대신 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 출생하다 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: In daily life use 태어나다; 출생하다 belongs to documents, news, and biographies. Telling a friend '저는 부산에서 출생했어요' sounds stiff, and '부산에서 태어났어요' is more natural. It also shows up in nouns like 출생지 (birthplace) and 출생 신고 (birth registration).

p.n: 태어나다 is the plain everyday word; 출생하다 is typical of formal writing.

examples.en: The expedition team set out toward the North Pole.
I joined the cave exploration team.

examples.ko: 탐험대원들이 지도 한 장만 들고 걸었어요.
examples.en: The members of the team walked with only a single map.
The expedition got lost in the jungle.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 친구들과 동네 탐험대를 만들어 놀았어요.
examples.en: As a child I played with friends by forming a neighborhood explorer club.
I wrote a letter of support to the polar expedition.

explain: '탐험대'는 여럿이 함께 가는 무리이고, 혼자 가는 사람은 '탐험가'라고 해요. 탐험대에 속한 사람 한 명은 '대원'이에요. 아이들 놀이에서는 '동네 탐험대'처럼 재미 삼아 이름을 붙이기도 해요.

phrases.en: I am a member of an expedition team that surveys mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탐험대에 속한 사람 한 명을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for one person who belongs to an expedition team.

phrases.en: My friends and I formed a neighborhood expedition team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들을 모아서 무리를 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means gathering people to form a group.

phrases.en: That explorer crossed the desert alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탐험대와 달리 혼자 탐험하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 탐험대, this refers to a person who explores alone.

explain_en: 탐험대 is a group that goes together, while a person who explores alone is a 탐험가. One member of the team is a 대원. In children's play, people sometimes name a game group like 동네 탐험대 just for fun.

en: to yell; to roar; to bawl

examples.en: Father yelled at my older brother who came home late.
The teacher bellowed at the students who were making noise.
An angry customer is yelling at the staff member.

examples.ko: 큰 소리로 호통치지 않아도 아이는 알아들어요.
examples.en: A child understands even if you don't bellow at them.

examples.ko: 사장님이 크게 호통치는 바람에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The boss roared so loudly that everyone was startled.
Grandmother may yell, but she soon laughs again.

explain: 주로 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 화가 나서 크게 소리를 지르며 꾸짖을 때 써요. '꾸짖다'보다 목소리가 크고 기세가 센 느낌이에요. '호통을 치다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The boss yelled at the employee.
phrases.nuance_ko: '호통치다'와 같은 뜻이고, '을'을 넣어 띄어 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'hotongchida'; it can also be written with 'eul' and a space.

phrases.en: I was late, so I got yelled at by my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야단을 맞는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person being scolded.

phrases.en: Please don't yell at the child like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령으로 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a negative request to stop someone.

explain_en: It is mostly used when someone in a higher position scolds a person below them in a loud, angry voice. It feels louder and more forceful than '꾸짖다'. You will also see it written as '호통을 치다'.
